3	The Validate intent playbook. Standalone — this intent critiques an existing PRD without changing it and ends after the user has seen the report; it does not run Finalize. The synthesis pipeline below is also reused for mid-session report requests during Create/Update.
4	
5	## Orient
6	
7	Source-extract against `.memlog.md`, any original inputs, and the PRD/addendum themselves. Delegate to subagents per PRD Discipline → "Extract, don't ingest" (in SKILL.md); the parent assembles from extracts.
8	
9	## Run the Reviewer Gate
10	
11	Run the Reviewer Gate (see SKILL.md) against `prd.md` (and `addendum.md` if present). The rubric walker is the default entry in the gate menu; under Validate intent it additionally runs the synthesis pipeline below. The Finalize discipline pass during Create/Update does NOT render a report — findings stay in-conversation.
12	
13	## Rubric-walker pipeline
14	
15	The rubric walker is the primary review entry. Spawn it as a subagent with this prompt:
16	
17	> You are validating a PRD against the quality rubric at `{workflow.validation_checklist_template}`. Read the full rubric first, then read `prd.md` (and `addendum.md` if present). Form a judgment per dimension — *strong / adequate / thin / broken* — and write findings only where they add information. Cite specific PRD locations and quote phrases. Severity ranks impact on the PRD's usefulness, not how easy the fix is. Write your review to `{doc_workspace}/review-rubric.md` in the format the rubric specifies. Return ONLY a compact summary (overall verdict, dimension verdicts, finding counts by severity, file path).
18	
19	The Reviewer Gate may also dispatch additional reviewers from `{workflow.finalize_reviewers}` (adversarial-general by default) and any ad-hoc reviewers the parent judges warranted. Each writes its review to `{doc_workspace}/review-{slug}.md` and returns a compact summary. Run in parallel.
20	
21	## Synthesis pipeline
22	
23	Once every selected reviewer has returned, the parent synthesizes one consolidated report. **Do not skip this step under Validate intent** — it produces the persistent artifact the user opens.
24	
25	### Inputs
26	
27	- `{doc_workspace}/review-rubric.md` — primary, structured by the seven dimensions
28	- Zero or more `{doc_workspace}/review-{slug}.md` files — extra reviewers (adversarial, etc.)
29	- `{workflow.validation_report_template}` — the HTML skeleton
30	
31	### What the synthesis pass does
32	
33	1. Read every reviewer file in `{doc_workspace}/review-*.md`.
34	2. Fill the HTML skeleton:
35	   - **Header.** PRD name, path. Grade derived from the rubric verdicts and severity counts: *Excellent* = all dimensions strong/adequate, no high/critical findings · *Good* = ≤1 thin dimension, no critical findings · *Fair* = multiple thin dimensions or any high finding · *Poor* = any broken dimension or any critical finding. Set the matching `grade-excellent | grade-good | grade-fair | grade-poor` class.
36	   - **Synthesis block.** Lift the rubric's *Overall verdict* paragraph as the lead; if adversarial or ad-hoc reviewers materially shift the picture, add a second paragraph that names what they surfaced.
37	   - **Dimension summary cards.** One per dimension that was assessed. Colored verdict text. Skip dimensions the rubric marked n/a for this PRD (e.g. downstream usability for a standalone PRD).
38	   - **Dimension sections.** One `<section class="dimension">` per assessed dimension, in rubric order. `<details open>` for *thin* and *broken*; closed for *strong* and *adequate*. Each contains the dimension judgment (the prose from review-rubric.md) and the findings list.
39	   - **Reviewer sections.** One `<section class="reviewer-section">` per extra reviewer that ran. The source file path goes in the `<span class="reviewer-source">`. Closed by default. Adversarial findings keep their adversarial voice — do not soften.
40	   - **Mechanical notes.** Bullet list from the rubric's "Mechanical notes" section. Skip the block if empty.
41	   - **Footer.** Rubric path, ISO timestamp.
42	3. Write the filled HTML to `{doc_workspace}/validation-report.html`.
43	4. Write the markdown twin to `{doc_workspace}/validation-report.md` (same content, grouped by severity rather than by dimension — see format below; this is the canonical form for downstream re-reading).
44	5. Open the HTML in the default browser with the platform opener — `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux, `start ""` on Windows — double-quoting the path:
45	   ```bash
46	   open "{doc_workspace}/validation-report.html"
47	   ```
48	   If the command fails, don't retry with another opener: tell the user the file path and move on. Skip the open step in headless mode (see `references/headless.md`).
49	
50	### Markdown twin format
51	
52	```markdown
53	# Validation Report — {prd_name}
54	
55	- **PRD:** `{prd_path}`
56	- **Rubric:** `{rubric_path}`
57	- **Run at:** {ISO timestamp}
58	- **Grade:** {Excellent | Good | Fair | Poor}
59	
60	## Overall verdict
61	{synthesis paragraphs}
62	
63	## Dimension verdicts
64	- Decision-readiness — {verdict}
65	- Substance over theater — {verdict}
66	- (etc. for each assessed dimension)
67	
68	## Findings by severity
69	
70	### Critical (n)
71	**[Dimension or Reviewer]** — Title (§ location)
72	{Note}
73	Fix: {suggested fix}
74	
75	### High (n)
76	...
77	
78	### Medium (n)
79	...
80	
81	### Low (n)
82	...
83	
84	## Mechanical notes
85	- {bullet}
86	
87	## Reviewer files
88	- `review-rubric.md`
89	- `review-adversarial-general.md` (if present)
90	- (etc.)
91	```
92	
93	Re-running validation overwrites the consolidated report in place. The individual `review-*.md` files are preserved so the user can drill in.
94	
95	## Close
96	
97	Surface artifact paths; the rendered HTML/markdown is the persistent artifact. Always offer to roll findings into an Update.

## Orient

Source-extract against `.memlog.md`, any original inputs, and the PRD/addendum themselves. Delegate to subagents per PRD Discipline → "Extract, don't ingest" (in SKILL.md); the parent assembles from extracts.

## Run the Reviewer Gate

Run the Reviewer Gate (see SKILL.md) against `prd.md` (and `addendum.md` if present). The rubric walker is the default entry in the gate menu; under Validate intent it additionally runs the synthesis pipeline below. The Finalize discipline pass during Create/Update does NOT render a report — findings stay in-conversation.

## Rubric-walker pipeline

The rubric walker is the primary review entry. Spawn it as a subagent with this prompt:

> You are validating a PRD against the quality rubric at `{workflow.validation_checklist_template}`. Read the full rubric first, then read `prd.md` (and `addendum.md` if present). Form a judgment per dimension — *strong / adequate / thin / broken* — and write findings only where they add information. Cite specific PRD locations and quote phrases. Severity ranks impact on the PRD's usefulness, not how easy the fix is. Write your review to `{doc_workspace}/review-rubric.md` in the format the rubric specifies. Return ONLY a compact summary (overall verdict, dimension verdicts, finding counts by severity, file path).

The Reviewer Gate may also dispatch additional reviewers from `{workflow.finalize_reviewers}` (adversarial-general by default) and any ad-hoc reviewers the parent judges warranted. Each writes its review to `{doc_workspace}/review-{slug}.md` and returns a compact summary. Run in parallel.

## Synthesis pipeline

Once every selected reviewer has returned, the parent synthesizes one consolidated report. **Do not skip this step under Validate intent** — it produces the persistent artifact the user opens.

### Inputs

- `{doc_workspace}/review-rubric.md` — primary, structured by the seven dimensions
- Zero or more `{doc_workspace}/review-{slug}.md` files — extra reviewers (adversarial, etc.)
- `{workflow.validation_report_template}` — the HTML skeleton

### What the synthesis pass does

1. Read every reviewer file in `{doc_workspace}/review-*.md`.
2. Fill the HTML skeleton:
   - **Header.** PRD name, path. Grade derived from the rubric verdicts and severity counts: *Excellent* = all dimensions strong/adequate, no high/critical findings · *Good* = ≤1 thin dimension, no critical findings · *Fair* = multiple thin dimensions or any high finding · *Poor* = any broken dimension or any critical finding. Set the matching `grade-excellent | grade-good | grade-fair | grade-poor` class.
   - **Synthesis block.** Lift the rubric's *Overall verdict* paragraph as the lead; if adversarial or ad-hoc reviewers materially shift the picture, add a second paragraph that names what they surfaced.
   - **Dimension summary cards.** One per dimension that was assessed. Colored verdict text. Skip dimensions the rubric marked n/a for this PRD (e.g. downstream usability for a standalone PRD).
   - **Dimension sections.** One `<section class="dimension">` per assessed dimension, in rubric order. `<details open>` for *thin* and *broken*; closed for *strong* and *adequate*. Each contains the dimension judgment (the prose from review-rubric.md) and the findings list.
   - **Reviewer sections.** One `<section class="reviewer-section">` per extra reviewer that ran. The source file path goes in the `<span class="reviewer-source">`. Closed by default. Adversarial findings keep their adversarial voice — do not soften.
   - **Mechanical notes.** Bullet list from the rubric's "Mechanical notes" section. Skip the block if empty.
   - **Footer.** Rubric path, ISO timestamp.
3. Write the filled HTML to `{doc_workspace}/validation-report.html`.
4. Write the markdown twin to `{doc_workspace}/validation-report.md` (same content, grouped by severity rather than by dimension — see format below; this is the canonical form for downstream re-reading).
5. Open the HTML in the default browser with the platform opener — `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux, `start ""` on Windows — double-quoting the path:
   ```bash
   open "{doc_workspace}/validation-report.html"
   ```
   If the command fails, don't retry with another opener: tell the user the file path and move on. Skip the open step in headless mode (see `references/headless.md`).

### Markdown twin format

```markdown
# Validation Report — {prd_name}

- **PRD:** `{prd_path}`
- **Rubric:** `{rubric_path}`
- **Run at:** {ISO timestamp}
- **Grade:** {Excellent | Good | Fair | Poor}

## Overall verdict
{synthesis paragraphs}

## Dimension verdicts
- Decision-readiness — {verdict}
- Substance over theater — {verdict}
- (etc. for each assessed dimension)

## Findings by severity

### Critical (n)
**[Dimension or Reviewer]** — Title (§ location)
{Note}
Fix: {suggested fix}

### High (n)
...

### Medium (n)
...

### Low (n)
...

## Mechanical notes
- {bullet}

## Reviewer files
- `review-rubric.md`
- `review-adversarial-general.md` (if present)
- (etc.)
```

Re-running validation overwrites the consolidated report in place. The individual `review-*.md` files are preserved so the user can drill in.

## Close

Surface artifact paths; the rendered HTML/markdown is the persistent artifact. Always offer to roll findings into an Update.

content.content:
1	# PRD Quality Rubric
2	
3	A judgment rubric for the validator subagent. Walk the PRD with these dimensions in mind and write substantive findings — not box-ticking. The goal is a review that tells the user whether this PRD is *good*, not whether it has the right section headers.
4	
5	Most PRDs do not need every dimension scrutinized equally. Calibrate to the agreed stakes, the PRD's shape (consumer product, internal tool, regulatory update, technical capability spec), and what the PRD itself is trying to do. Be specific — cite locations, quote phrases, name what's missing. Abstract criticism is failure of nerve.
6	
7	## How to use this rubric
8	
9	1. Read the full PRD (and addendum.md if present) before writing anything.
10	2. For each of the seven dimensions below, form a judgment — *strong / adequate / thin / broken* — backed by specifics from the PRD.
11	3. Write findings only where they add information. A `strong` dimension may need no findings; a `broken` one needs concrete, fixable ones.
12	4. Severity ranks impact on the PRD's usefulness, not how easy the fix is. A vague Vision statement is *critical* even though it's a one-paragraph fix; a glossary drift might be *low* even though it appears in many places.
13	5. The overall verdict is your synthesis — 2–3 sentences that name what holds up and what's at risk. Earn it with the dimension judgments.
14	
15	## Output format
16	
17	Write findings to `{doc_workspace}/review-rubric.md`:
18	
19	```markdown
20	# PRD Quality Review — {prd_name}
21	
22	## Overall verdict
23	[2–3 sentences. What holds up, what's at risk. Earned by the dimension judgments below.]
24	
25	## Decision-readiness — [strong | adequate | thin | broken]
26	[1–3 paragraphs of judgment with specific PRD locations.]
27	
28	### Findings
29	- **[critical|high|medium|low]** [Title] (§ location) — [Note]. *Fix:* [suggested fix].
30	
31	## Substance over theater — [verdict]
32	...
33	
34	(repeat for each dimension)
35	
36	## Mechanical notes
37	[Glossary drift, ID continuity, broken cross-refs, Assumptions Index roundtrip. Lighter weight — these matter for downstream but don't drive the overall verdict.]
38	```
39	
40	## The seven dimensions
41	
42	### 1. Decision-readiness
43	
44	Can a decision-maker act on this PRD? Are the trade-offs surfaced honestly, or has the PRD smoothed everything to neutral? Would someone pushing back find their objection acknowledged or dodged?
45	
46	Look for:
47	- Decisions that are stated as decisions, not buried as "considerations."
48	- Trade-offs named with what was given up, not just what was chosen.
49	- Open Questions that are actually open — not rhetorical questions with an answer in the next sentence.
50	- `[NOTE FOR PM]` callouts at real tensions, not at safe checkpoints.
51	
52	Red flag: a PRD where every choice "balances" everything, every NFR is "important," every persona "values" the product.
53	
54	### 2. Substance over theater
55	
56	Is the content earned, or is it furniture? Distinguish:
57	
58	- **Persona theater** — Personas that don't drive a single decision in the PRD. More than four personas. Personas whose only function is to make the PRD look thorough.
59	- **Innovation theater** — claimed novelty that isn't novel. Differentiation sections written because the template had one, not because Discovery surfaced something.
60	- **NFR theater** — copied boilerplate ("system must be scalable / secure / reliable") without product-specific thresholds.
61	- **Vision theater** — a Vision statement that could swap into any PRD in this category without change.
62	
63	Flag what reads like furniture, even if it's well-written furniture.
64	
65	### 3. Strategic coherence
66	
67	Does the PRD have a thesis? Do the features serve a unified arc, or is it a list of capabilities someone wanted?
68	
69	Look for:
70	- A stated thesis the PRD bets on (problem framing, user insight, market move).
71	- Feature prioritization that follows from the thesis — not from "what's easy first."
72	- Success Metrics that validate the thesis, not metrics that just measure activity (DAU/MAU when the thesis is about engagement quality is a tell).
73	- Counter-metrics named when SMs exist.
74	- Coherent MVP scope kind — problem-solving, experience, platform, or revenue — with scope logic that matches.
75	
76	Red flag: a PRD that reads as a backlog with section headings.
77	
78	### 4. Done-ness clarity
79	
80	Would an engineer reading this PRD know what "done" looks like for each FR?
81	
82	Look for:
83	- FRs with at least one testable consequence per FR — verifiable condition, measurable outcome.
84	- "System handles X gracefully," "reasonable performance," "user-friendly" — flag every one.
85	- Acceptance criteria implied or explicit. Sometimes the FR's consequences carry this; sometimes the PRD genuinely needs an Acceptance section.
86	- For non-functional sections (UX, performance, security): bounds, not adjectives.
87	
88	This is the dimension downstream story creation will lean on hardest. Be unforgiving here.
89	
90	### 5. Scope honesty
91	
92	Are omissions explicit, or is the reader meant to infer them?
93	
94	Look for:
95	- A Non-Goals section where it would do real work — and `[NON-GOAL for MVP]` callouts where omissions could be silently assumed.
96	- `[ASSUMPTION: …]` tags on inferences the user didn't directly confirm, indexed at the end.
97	- `[NOTE FOR PM]` callouts at deferred decisions and unresolved tensions.
98	- De-scoping proposed honestly, not done silently.
99	
100	Open-items density: count Open Questions + `[ASSUMPTION]` + `[NOTE FOR PM]` callouts relative to stakes. High counts on a low-stakes PRD is fine; high counts on a green-light-to-build PRD is a blocker.
101	
102	### 6. Downstream usability
103	
104	If this PRD feeds UX, architecture, or story creation, can those workflows source-extract from it cleanly?
105	
106	Look for:
107	- Glossary present; every domain noun used identically across FRs, UJs, SM definitions.
108	- FR / UJ / SM IDs contiguous, unique, and cross-references that resolve.
109	- Each section makes sense pulled out alone — cross-references via Glossary terms, not "see above."
110	- UJs each have a named protagonist; no floating UJs.
111	
112	For standalone PRDs (no downstream), this dimension matters less — say so.
113	
114	### 7. Shape fit
115	
116	Has the PRD been forced into a shape that doesn't match the product?
117	
118	- Consumer product / multi-stakeholder B2B / meaningful UX → UJs with named protagonists are load-bearing.
119	- Internal tool, single-operator role → capability spec shape; UJs may be overhead; SMs may be operational rather than user-facing.
120	- Regulatory or compliance update → constraint traceability is non-negotiable; UJs may be irrelevant.
121	- Hobby / solo → rigor light, substance bar still applies.
122	- Brownfield → existing-code references must be accurate; new UJs and existing UJs must be distinguished.
123	- Chain-top (feeds UX → architecture → stories) → downstream usability matters more; standalone PRDs can be lighter on traceability.
124	
125	Flag PRDs that are over-formalized (UJ density for a single-operator tool) or under-formalized (consumer product with no UJs).
126	
127	## Mechanical notes
128	
129	Cover these as a tail section, not a primary dimension. They matter for downstream but don't drive the verdict on whether the PRD is good.
130

# PRD Quality Rubric

A judgment rubric for the validator subagent. Walk the PRD with these dimensions in mind and write substantive findings — not box-ticking. The goal is a review that tells the user whether this PRD is *good*, not whether it has the right section headers.

Most PRDs do not need every dimension scrutinized equally. Calibrate to the agreed stakes, the PRD's shape (consumer product, internal tool, regulatory update, technical capability spec), and what the PRD itself is trying to do. Be specific — cite locations, quote phrases, name what's missing. Abstract criticism is failure of nerve.

## How to use this rubric

1. Read the full PRD (and addendum.md if present) before writing anything.
2. For each of the seven dimensions below, form a judgment — *strong / adequate / thin / broken* — backed by specifics from the PRD.
3. Write findings only where they add information. A `strong` dimension may need no findings; a `broken` one needs concrete, fixable ones.
4. Severity ranks impact on the PRD's usefulness, not how easy the fix is. A vague Vision statement is *critical* even though it's a one-paragraph fix; a glossary drift might be *low* even though it appears in many places.
5. The overall verdict is your synthesis — 2–3 sentences that name what holds up and what's at risk. Earn it with the dimension judgments.

## Output format

Write findings to `{doc_workspace}/review-rubric.md`:

```markdown
# PRD Quality Review — {prd_name}

## Overall verdict
[2–3 sentences. What holds up, what's at risk. Earned by the dimension judgments below.]

## Decision-readiness — [strong | adequate | thin | broken]
[1–3 paragraphs of judgment with specific PRD locations.]

### Findings
- **[critical|high|medium|low]** [Title] (§ location) — [Note]. *Fix:* [suggested fix].

## Substance over theater — [verdict]
...

(repeat for each dimension)

## Mechanical notes
[Glossary drift, ID continuity, broken cross-refs, Assumptions Index roundtrip. Lighter weight — these matter for downstream but don't drive the overall verdict.]
```

## The seven dimensions

### 1. Decision-readiness

Can a decision-maker act on this PRD? Are the trade-offs surfaced honestly, or has the PRD smoothed everything to neutral? Would someone pushing back find their objection acknowledged or dodged?

Look for:
- Decisions that are stated as decisions, not buried as "considerations."
- Trade-offs named with what was given up, not just what was chosen.
- Open Questions that are actually open — not rhetorical questions with an answer in the next sentence.
- `[NOTE FOR PM]` callouts at real tensions, not at safe checkpoints.

Red flag: a PRD where every choice "balances" everything, every NFR is "important," every persona "values" the product.

### 2. Substance over theater

Is the content earned, or is it furniture? Distinguish:

- **Persona theater** — Personas that don't drive a single decision in the PRD. More than four personas. Personas whose only function is to make the PRD look thorough.
- **Innovation theater** — claimed novelty that isn't novel. Differentiation sections written because the template had one, not because Discovery surfaced something.
- **NFR theater** — copied boilerplate ("system must be scalable / secure / reliable") without product-specific thresholds.
- **Vision theater** — a Vision statement that could swap into any PRD in this category without change.

Flag what reads like furniture, even if it's well-written furniture.

### 3. Strategic coherence

Does the PRD have a thesis? Do the features serve a unified arc, or is it a list of capabilities someone wanted?

Look for:
- A stated thesis the PRD bets on (problem framing, user insight, market move).
- Feature prioritization that follows from the thesis — not from "what's easy first."
- Success Metrics that validate the thesis, not metrics that just measure activity (DAU/MAU when the thesis is about engagement quality is a tell).
- Counter-metrics named when SMs exist.
- Coherent MVP scope kind — problem-solving, experience, platform, or revenue — with scope logic that matches.

Red flag: a PRD that reads as a backlog with section headings.

### 4. Done-ness clarity

Would an engineer reading this PRD know what "done" looks like for each FR?

Look for:
- FRs with at least one testable consequence per FR — verifiable condition, measurable outcome.
- "System handles X gracefully," "reasonable performance," "user-friendly" — flag every one.
- Acceptance criteria implied or explicit. Sometimes the FR's consequences carry this; sometimes the PRD genuinely needs an Acceptance section.
- For non-functional sections (UX, performance, security): bounds, not adjectives.

This is the dimension downstream story creation will lean on hardest. Be unforgiving here.

### 5. Scope honesty

Are omissions explicit, or is the reader meant to infer them?

Look for:
- A Non-Goals section where it would do real work — and `[NON-GOAL for MVP]` callouts where omissions could be silently assumed.
- `[ASSUMPTION: …]` tags on inferences the user didn't directly confirm, indexed at the end.
- `[NOTE FOR PM]` callouts at deferred decisions and unresolved tensions.
- De-scoping proposed honestly, not done silently.

Open-items density: count Open Questions + `[ASSUMPTION]` + `[NOTE FOR PM]` callouts relative to stakes. High counts on a low-stakes PRD is fine; high counts on a green-light-to-build PRD is a blocker.

### 6. Downstream usability

If this PRD feeds UX, architecture, or story creation, can those workflows source-extract from it cleanly?

Look for:
- Glossary present; every domain noun used identically across FRs, UJs, SM definitions.
- FR / UJ / SM IDs contiguous, unique, and cross-references that resolve.
- Each section makes sense pulled out alone — cross-references via Glossary terms, not "see above."
- UJs each have a named protagonist; no floating UJs.

For standalone PRDs (no downstream), this dimension matters less — say so.

### 7. Shape fit

Has the PRD been forced into a shape that doesn't match the product?

- Consumer product / multi-stakeholder B2B / meaningful UX → UJs with named protagonists are load-bearing.
- Internal tool, single-operator role → capability spec shape; UJs may be overhead; SMs may be operational rather than user-facing.
- Regulatory or compliance update → constraint traceability is non-negotiable; UJs may be irrelevant.
- Hobby / solo → rigor light, substance bar still applies.
- Brownfield → existing-code references must be accurate; new UJs and existing UJs must be distinguished.
- Chain-top (feeds UX → architecture → stories) → downstream usability matters more; standalone PRDs can be lighter on traceability.

Flag PRDs that are over-formalized (UJ density for a single-operator tool) or under-formalized (consumer product with no UJs).

## Mechanical notes

Cover these as a tail section, not a primary dimension. They matter for downstream but don't drive the verdict on whether the PRD is good.

- Glossary drift (case, plural, synonyms across the PRD).
- ID continuity (gaps, duplicates, unresolved cross-references).
- Assumptions Index roundtrip (every inline `[ASSUMPTION]` indexed; index entries all appear inline).
- UJ protagonist naming (each UJ has a named protagonist carrying context inline).
- Required sections present for the agreed stakes and product type.

1	# PRD Quality Review — Cerne
2	
3	## Overall verdict
4	
5	This is an unusually honest, well-disciplined PRD for its stakes: its Open Questions, `[ASSUMPTION]` tags, and Non-Goals do real work instead of performing completeness, its 43 FRs / 6 UJs / IDs are contiguous and cross-reference cleanly, and the Cross-Cutting NFRs and Failure-contract table are specific enough to be checked, not adjectives. The two real soft spots are **done-ness** — a handful of FRs (FR-11, FR-15, FR-20) and one NFR (RNF01) have no settled acceptance path despite `status: final` — and **strategic coherence** — RF08 (Proactive Insights) is the one feature with no stated User-Journey anchor, the single break in an otherwise-complete thesis→UJ→feature chain. Neither defect is fatal or expensive to close, but both are exactly the kind of thing a solo author should resolve deliberately before build reaches those units, not discover mid-implementation.
6	
7	## Decision-readiness — strong
8	
9	Decisions are stated as decisions (§1's "bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory"), trade-offs name what was given up (FR-20: "no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature"), and §8's eleven Open Questions mostly read as genuinely unresolved rather than rhetorical — several are wired directly into the FR they block (`[OPEN]` tags inline at FR-11, FR-15, FR-20), which is exactly the behavior the rubric wants instead of a quiet gap. SM-5 is explicitly marked "informal" and "not a graded criterion" rather than dressed up as a real metric. The one `[NOTE FOR PM]` (§4.11, under FR-43) sits at a real tension — a missing account-deletion confirmation screen — not a safe checkpoint.
10	
11	### Findings
12	
13	- **medium** Open Questions aren't sequenced against the delivery order they constrain (§8, §6.1) — OQ-3 blocks FR-11 inside RF01 (build unit 2 of 11) and OQ-7 blocks FR-19/20 inside RF06 (unit 6), but §8 lists all eleven OQs as a flat, unprioritized numbered list with no marker for "must resolve before unit N starts." A solo author sequencing their own work benefits from knowing which OQs are load-bearing soon vs. deferrable to polish time. *Fix:* tag each OQ with the earliest build unit it blocks, or sort §8 by urgency against §6.1's order.
14	- **low** OQ-5 ("Cloud-only, immutable-entry design is a backend constraint... confirm there's no appetite to request a contract change") is not actually open — the same sentence answers it ("there is none per `AGENTS.md`"). The PRD is self-aware about this ("recorded here only so it isn't silently re-discovered as a bug later"), so the risk is cosmetic, but it inflates the "genuinely open" count a reader would use to gauge readiness. *Fix:* move OQ-5 to a "Decisions already settled, recorded for visibility" note rather than the Open Questions list.
15	
16	## Substance over theater — strong
17	
18	No findings. The persona is a single, consistently-named protagonist (Mara) reused across all six UJs rather than a persona roster assembled for appearance. The Cross-Cutting NFRs are quantified (RNF01: "<100ms" / "300ms"; RNF07: "≥80%"; RNF08: "zero hardcoded visual values") rather than boilerplate ("must be scalable/secure"). The Vision (§1) is specific to this product's bet and the addendum's competitive section names real, specific competitor complaints (Mindsera "feature-sprawl," Rosebud's "therapist-designed framing risk") rather than generic differentiation language — this reads as earned, not templated.
19	
20	## Strategic coherence — adequate
21	
22	The thesis ("a better memory," §1) is stated plainly and every feature section but one explicitly declares which UJ it realizes, which is the right mechanism for proving a PRD isn't a backlog with headers. Success Metrics are honestly scoped to conformance rather than adoption, and the PRD says so itself (§7: "this PRD's graded metrics (SM-1–3) can only confirm the RAG-memory mechanism is wired correctly end-to-end... is not a graded surface for this delivery") — for an academic-stakes deliverable this is the right call, explicitly owned rather than smoothed over.
23	
24	### Findings
25	
26	- **medium** §4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08 / FR-31–33) is the only feature section that does not declare a "Realizes UJ-X" linkage — every other section in §4 does (4.1 through 4.8, 4.10, 4.11 all state one). RF08's description reads "Depends on RF04" and stops. This breaks the otherwise-complete thesis→UJ→feature traceability chain the rest of the document relies on, and leaves FR-31–33 structurally un-anchored to any user journey. *Fix:* either add a UJ realized by RF08 (e.g., extend UJ-2 to cover an unprompted Insight arriving mid-conversation, which the current UJ-2 edge case does not mention), or state explicitly that RF08 is UJ-less by design and why.
27	
28	## Done-ness clarity — adequate
29	
30	Most FRs carry a single self-evident testable clause or an explicit Consequences block, and several are impressively concrete (FR-38's "correctly at zero, one, and more-than-thirty Entries"; FR-21's "debounced... by 300ms"; FR-31's "5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity, whichever occurs first"). None of the classic vague tells ("gracefully," "reasonable," "user-friendly") appear in an FR statement. But a non-trivial slice of the 43 FRs, plus one NFR, do not actually have a settled "done" at this status.
31	
32	### Findings
33	
34	- **high** RNF01 (performance: "<100ms" local UI, "300ms" loading-indicator threshold) is the only one of the nine Cross-Cutting NFRs with no mapped Success Metric or stated verification method. SM-2 explicitly ties to RNF06+RNF07, SM-3 to RNF09, SM-4 to RNF08 — but no SM references RNF01, and §7 gives no instrumented or manual method (profiling pass? instrumented test? stopwatch?) for checking it. For a document whose whole Success Metrics framing is "success is defined by specification conformance" (§7), a conformance criterion with no check is a gap. *Fix:* either add an SM (or a line under SM-1) that names how RNF01 gets verified, or state explicitly that RNF01 is unverified-by-design for this delivery.
35	- **medium** Three FRs have a literal unresolved sub-behavior at `status: final`: FR-11 ("`[OPEN]` Switching tabs mid-recording... is undefined behavior in the current prototype"), FR-15 ("`[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state"), and FR-20 ("`[OPEN]` How an active text search and active filters interact... is unspecified"). These are honestly flagged (good — this is exactly what explicit scope-honesty should look like), but it means an engineer building RF01 (unit 2 of 11) or RF06 (unit 6) cannot fully determine "done" for that sub-behavior without first resolving OQ-3/OQ-6/OQ-7. *Fix:* no PRD change needed beyond what §8 already does — but see the Decision-readiness finding above about sequencing these against build order, since FR-11's gap is live almost immediately.
36	- **medium** FR-19 (Semantic search) states the behavior with an example ("'ansiedade' matches... 'nervosismo'") but, unlike RF05/RF08/RF09 which each explicitly declare generated-content *quality* out of acceptance scope (§5: "Grading or verifying the quality of AI-generated text... RF05/RF08/RF09 are scoped to mechanism... quality is explicitly out of acceptance scope"), RF06 search-result quality has no such explicit carve-out. §8 OQ-10 raises this exact "mechanism-only" boundary question for RF04 only — RF06 has the identical ambiguity (is "returns semantically correct results" part of what's graded, or only "calls the endpoint and renders whatever comes back"?) and it isn't named anywhere. *Fix:* extend OQ-10 (or add an OQ-12) to cover RF06 search-quality alongside RF04 chat-quality.
37	- **low** RNF02 ("PII stripping runs via a Claude Haiku 4.5... step, server-side only") and RNF03 ("Zero data retention by upstream AI providers") describe backend/vendor facts the Flutter app neither implements nor can verify — they're inherited context, not app-testable requirements, yet they sit in the same "Cross-Cutting NFRs" list as RNF01/04/05-09 which *are* app behaviors. This blurs what this PRD's own deliverable is actually on the hook for. *Fix:* either mark RNF02/RNF03 as "inherited, not verified by this delivery" inline, or move them to the addendum's backend-context section alongside the "tech stack already fixed upstream" note (which already does this for the AI models themselves).
38	
39	## Scope honesty — strong
40	
41	The Non-Goals section (§5) does real work — eight explicit exclusions, three tagged `[ext]` and tied to concrete inert-placeholder descriptions (e.g., persona adjustment "exists only as a cosmetic Settings selector... that does not change assistant behavior in this delivery"), plus the risk-signal-detection exclusion is framed as "a deliberate scope exclusion... not an oversight." The two `[ASSUMPTION]` tags (§2.1/§2.3 persona reconstruction, §4.1 FR-1 signup fields) both round-trip cleanly into §9's Assumptions Index with no orphaned or missing entries. De-scoping is proposed openly rather than silently assumed (§5's AI-categorization and goal-extraction items both state what they're downgraded to, not just that they're cut).
42	
43	No additional findings beyond what's already captured under Decision-readiness (OQ-5 mislabeling) and Done-ness clarity (the FR-11/15/20 `[OPEN]` tags) — both are scope-honesty mechanisms working as intended, not failures of this dimension.
44	
45	## Downstream usability — strong
46	
47	Glossary (§3) terms are used consistently as proper nouns through the FRs (Entry, Chat Session, Chat Message, Sync Badge, Export Job). FR IDs run FR-1 through FR-43 with no gaps or duplicates (verified by section-by-section count: 3+4+4+2+5+4+5+3+3+4+6 = 43, matching §0's stated range); UJ-1 through UJ-6 and SM-1–5 plus SM-C1/C2 are likewise contiguous. Cross-references resolve on spot-check (FR-15→FR-17, the error-taxonomy table's FR-37/FR-13 references, UJ-2's FR-2/FR-26 citation) and the Failure-contract retryable-code list is consistent across three locations (the PRD's own table, §7 SM-3's "5×3=15" framing, and the addendum's dio-retry list) — all six retryable codes match exactly across all three. Each feature section (§4.1–§4.11) is reasonably self-contained, stating its own dependencies and UJ linkage inline rather than relying on "see above."
48	
49	## Shape fit — strong
50	
51	This is a consumer product with meaningful UX, and UJs with a named, consistent protagonist (Mara) are correctly load-bearing — six UJs, one per major feature cluster, neither over- nor under-formalized. The heavy formal apparatus (43 FRs, a 13-code failure taxonomy, explicit NFR thresholds) matches the stated "academic/TCC rigorous" stakes and the stated audience (§0: "the solo author... and the academic reviewers who evaluate it") rather than being over-built for a solo hobby project — the rigor is calibrated to who grades it. Greenfield framing is handled correctly (no stale brownfield references; §0 and AGENTS.md agree no Flutter project exists yet). As a chain-top document (feeds UX/architecture/story work, §0), the downstream-usability strength above is load-bearing and earned.
52	
53	## Mechanical notes
54	
55	- **Casing drift:** "Entry" is capitalized consistently as the Glossary-defined term through most of §4, but §5's Non-Goals heading text drifts to lowercase ("Dynamic AI categorization of **entries**," "Offline **entry** creation"). Similarly "Dashboard" is capitalized in §3's Glossary but appears lowercase through §4.11 and UJ-6 ("checks her settings **dashboard**"). Low-impact, but worth a pass before downstream extraction treats case as meaningful.
56	- **Unnumbered sections:** §0–§9 are numbered, but "Information Architecture" (between §3 and §4) and the three trailing sections (Cross-Cutting NFRs, Constraints and Guardrails, Aesthetic and Tone) carry no section numbers. Internal references to the latter use the section name as a pseudo-ID (e.g., FR-18's "see §Cross-Cutting NFRs" convention), which works but is inconsistent with the rest of the document's numeric cross-referencing.
57	- **Feature-specific NFR without an ID:** §4.5's BLoC-composition rule ("No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly...") is referenced by SM-1 but, unlike the nine global RNF01–09, has no stable identifier of its own. If more feature-specific NFRs accumulate, this will need one to stay unambiguous under downstream extraction.
58	- **Assumptions Index and ID continuity otherwise check out clean:** both `[ASSUMPTION]` tags round-trip into §9 with no drift; FR/UJ/SM numbering has no gaps, duplicates, or unresolved forward references found on spot-check.

# PRD Quality Review — Cerne

## Overall verdict

This is an unusually honest, well-disciplined PRD for its stakes: its Open Questions, `[ASSUMPTION]` tags, and Non-Goals do real work instead of performing completeness, its 43 FRs / 6 UJs / IDs are contiguous and cross-reference cleanly, and the Cross-Cutting NFRs and Failure-contract table are specific enough to be checked, not adjectives. The two real soft spots are **done-ness** — a handful of FRs (FR-11, FR-15, FR-20) and one NFR (RNF01) have no settled acceptance path despite `status: final` — and **strategic coherence** — RF08 (Proactive Insights) is the one feature with no stated User-Journey anchor, the single break in an otherwise-complete thesis→UJ→feature chain. Neither defect is fatal or expensive to close, but both are exactly the kind of thing a solo author should resolve deliberately before build reaches those units, not discover mid-implementation.

## Decision-readiness — strong

Decisions are stated as decisions (§1's "bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory"), trade-offs name what was given up (FR-20: "no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature"), and §8's eleven Open Questions mostly read as genuinely unresolved rather than rhetorical — several are wired directly into the FR they block (`[OPEN]` tags inline at FR-11, FR-15, FR-20), which is exactly the behavior the rubric wants instead of a quiet gap. SM-5 is explicitly marked "informal" and "not a graded criterion" rather than dressed up as a real metric. The one `[NOTE FOR PM]` (§4.11, under FR-43) sits at a real tension — a missing account-deletion confirmation screen — not a safe checkpoint.

### Findings

- **medium** Open Questions aren't sequenced against the delivery order they constrain (§8, §6.1) — OQ-3 blocks FR-11 inside RF01 (build unit 2 of 11) and OQ-7 blocks FR-19/20 inside RF06 (unit 6), but §8 lists all eleven OQs as a flat, unprioritized numbered list with no marker for "must resolve before unit N starts." A solo author sequencing their own work benefits from knowing which OQs are load-bearing soon vs. deferrable to polish time. *Fix:* tag each OQ with the earliest build unit it blocks, or sort §8 by urgency against §6.1's order.
- **low** OQ-5 ("Cloud-only, immutable-entry design is a backend constraint... confirm there's no appetite to request a contract change") is not actually open — the same sentence answers it ("there is none per `AGENTS.md`"). The PRD is self-aware about this ("recorded here only so it isn't silently re-discovered as a bug later"), so the risk is cosmetic, but it inflates the "genuinely open" count a reader would use to gauge readiness. *Fix:* move OQ-5 to a "Decisions already settled, recorded for visibility" note rather than the Open Questions list.

## Substance over theater — strong

No findings. The persona is a single, consistently-named protagonist (Mara) reused across all six UJs rather than a persona roster assembled for appearance. The Cross-Cutting NFRs are quantified (RNF01: "<100ms" / "300ms"; RNF07: "≥80%"; RNF08: "zero hardcoded visual values") rather than boilerplate ("must be scalable/secure"). The Vision (§1) is specific to this product's bet and the addendum's competitive section names real, specific competitor complaints (Mindsera "feature-sprawl," Rosebud's "therapist-designed framing risk") rather than generic differentiation language — this reads as earned, not templated.

## Strategic coherence — adequate

The thesis ("a better memory," §1) is stated plainly and every feature section but one explicitly declares which UJ it realizes, which is the right mechanism for proving a PRD isn't a backlog with headers. Success Metrics are honestly scoped to conformance rather than adoption, and the PRD says so itself (§7: "this PRD's graded metrics (SM-1–3) can only confirm the RAG-memory mechanism is wired correctly end-to-end... is not a graded surface for this delivery") — for an academic-stakes deliverable this is the right call, explicitly owned rather than smoothed over.

### Findings

- **medium** §4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08 / FR-31–33) is the only feature section that does not declare a "Realizes UJ-X" linkage — every other section in §4 does (4.1 through 4.8, 4.10, 4.11 all state one). RF08's description reads "Depends on RF04" and stops. This breaks the otherwise-complete thesis→UJ→feature traceability chain the rest of the document relies on, and leaves FR-31–33 structurally un-anchored to any user journey. *Fix:* either add a UJ realized by RF08 (e.g., extend UJ-2 to cover an unprompted Insight arriving mid-conversation, which the current UJ-2 edge case does not mention), or state explicitly that RF08 is UJ-less by design and why.

## Done-ness clarity — adequate

Most FRs carry a single self-evident testable clause or an explicit Consequences block, and several are impressively concrete (FR-38's "correctly at zero, one, and more-than-thirty Entries"; FR-21's "debounced... by 300ms"; FR-31's "5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity, whichever occurs first"). None of the classic vague tells ("gracefully," "reasonable," "user-friendly") appear in an FR statement. But a non-trivial slice of the 43 FRs, plus one NFR, do not actually have a settled "done" at this status.

### Findings

- **high** RNF01 (performance: "<100ms" local UI, "300ms" loading-indicator threshold) is the only one of the nine Cross-Cutting NFRs with no mapped Success Metric or stated verification method. SM-2 explicitly ties to RNF06+RNF07, SM-3 to RNF09, SM-4 to RNF08 — but no SM references RNF01, and §7 gives no instrumented or manual method (profiling pass? instrumented test? stopwatch?) for checking it. For a document whose whole Success Metrics framing is "success is defined by specification conformance" (§7), a conformance criterion with no check is a gap. *Fix:* either add an SM (or a line under SM-1) that names how RNF01 gets verified, or state explicitly that RNF01 is unverified-by-design for this delivery.
- **medium** Three FRs have a literal unresolved sub-behavior at `status: final`: FR-11 ("`[OPEN]` Switching tabs mid-recording... is undefined behavior in the current prototype"), FR-15 ("`[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state"), and FR-20 ("`[OPEN]` How an active text search and active filters interact... is unspecified"). These are honestly flagged (good — this is exactly what explicit scope-honesty should look like), but it means an engineer building RF01 (unit 2 of 11) or RF06 (unit 6) cannot fully determine "done" for that sub-behavior without first resolving OQ-3/OQ-6/OQ-7. *Fix:* no PRD change needed beyond what §8 already does — but see the Decision-readiness finding above about sequencing these against build order, since FR-11's gap is live almost immediately.
- **medium** FR-19 (Semantic search) states the behavior with an example ("'ansiedade' matches... 'nervosismo'") but, unlike RF05/RF08/RF09 which each explicitly declare generated-content *quality* out of acceptance scope (§5: "Grading or verifying the quality of AI-generated text... RF05/RF08/RF09 are scoped to mechanism... quality is explicitly out of acceptance scope"), RF06 search-result quality has no such explicit carve-out. §8 OQ-10 raises this exact "mechanism-only" boundary question for RF04 only — RF06 has the identical ambiguity (is "returns semantically correct results" part of what's graded, or only "calls the endpoint and renders whatever comes back"?) and it isn't named anywhere. *Fix:* extend OQ-10 (or add an OQ-12) to cover RF06 search-quality alongside RF04 chat-quality.
- **low** RNF02 ("PII stripping runs via a Claude Haiku 4.5... step, server-side only") and RNF03 ("Zero data retention by upstream AI providers") describe backend/vendor facts the Flutter app neither implements nor can verify — they're inherited context, not app-testable requirements, yet they sit in the same "Cross-Cutting NFRs" list as RNF01/04/05-09 which *are* app behaviors. This blurs what this PRD's own deliverable is actually on the hook for. *Fix:* either mark RNF02/RNF03 as "inherited, not verified by this delivery" inline, or move them to the addendum's backend-context section alongside the "tech stack already fixed upstream" note (which already does this for the AI models themselves).

## Scope honesty — strong

The Non-Goals section (§5) does real work — eight explicit exclusions, three tagged `[ext]` and tied to concrete inert-placeholder descriptions (e.g., persona adjustment "exists only as a cosmetic Settings selector... that does not change assistant behavior in this delivery"), plus the risk-signal-detection exclusion is framed as "a deliberate scope exclusion... not an oversight." The two `[ASSUMPTION]` tags (§2.1/§2.3 persona reconstruction, §4.1 FR-1 signup fields) both round-trip cleanly into §9's Assumptions Index with no orphaned or missing entries. De-scoping is proposed openly rather than silently assumed (§5's AI-categorization and goal-extraction items both state what they're downgraded to, not just that they're cut).

No additional findings beyond what's already captured under Decision-readiness (OQ-5 mislabeling) and Done-ness clarity (the FR-11/15/20 `[OPEN]` tags) — both are scope-honesty mechanisms working as intended, not failures of this dimension.

## Downstream usability — strong

Glossary (§3) terms are used consistently as proper nouns through the FRs (Entry, Chat Session, Chat Message, Sync Badge, Export Job). FR IDs run FR-1 through FR-43 with no gaps or duplicates (verified by section-by-section count: 3+4+4+2+5+4+5+3+3+4+6 = 43, matching §0's stated range); UJ-1 through UJ-6 and SM-1–5 plus SM-C1/C2 are likewise contiguous. Cross-references resolve on spot-check (FR-15→FR-17, the error-taxonomy table's FR-37/FR-13 references, UJ-2's FR-2/FR-26 citation) and the Failure-contract retryable-code list is consistent across three locations (the PRD's own table, §7 SM-3's "5×3=15" framing, and the addendum's dio-retry list) — all six retryable codes match exactly across all three. Each feature section (§4.1–§4.11) is reasonably self-contained, stating its own dependencies and UJ linkage inline rather than relying on "see above."

## Shape fit — strong

This is a consumer product with meaningful UX, and UJs with a named, consistent protagonist (Mara) are correctly load-bearing — six UJs, one per major feature cluster, neither over- nor under-formalized. The heavy formal apparatus (43 FRs, a 13-code failure taxonomy, explicit NFR thresholds) matches the stated "academic/TCC rigorous" stakes and the stated audience (§0: "the solo author... and the academic reviewers who evaluate it") rather than being over-built for a solo hobby project — the rigor is calibrated to who grades it. Greenfield framing is handled correctly (no stale brownfield references; §0 and AGENTS.md agree no Flutter project exists yet). As a chain-top document (feeds UX/architecture/story work, §0), the downstream-usability strength above is load-bearing and earned.

## Mechanical notes

- **Casing drift:** "Entry" is capitalized consistently as the Glossary-defined term through most of §4, but §5's Non-Goals heading text drifts to lowercase ("Dynamic AI categorization of **entries**," "Offline **entry** creation"). Similarly "Dashboard" is capitalized in §3's Glossary but appears lowercase through §4.11 and UJ-6 ("checks her settings **dashboard**"). Low-impact, but worth a pass before downstream extraction treats case as meaningful.
- **Unnumbered sections:** §0–§9 are numbered, but "Information Architecture" (between §3 and §4) and the three trailing sections (Cross-Cutting NFRs, Constraints and Guardrails, Aesthetic and Tone) carry no section numbers. Internal references to the latter use the section name as a pseudo-ID (e.g., FR-18's "see §Cross-Cutting NFRs" convention), which works but is inconsistent with the rest of the document's numeric cross-referencing.
- **Feature-specific NFR without an ID:** §4.5's BLoC-composition rule ("No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly...") is referenced by SM-1 but, unlike the nine global RNF01–09, has no stable identifier of its own. If more feature-specific NFRs accumulate, this will need one to stay unambiguous under downstream extraction.
- **Assumptions Index and ID continuity otherwise check out clean:** both `[ASSUMPTION]` tags round-trip into §9 with no drift; FR/UJ/SM numbering has no gaps, duplicates, or unresolved forward references found on spot-check.

20	## 1. Vision
21	
22	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app whose AI assistant actually remembers the user. The user captures their day by text, voice, or photo; a conversational agent then answers using retrieval-augmented generation over that person's own past entries — not the stateless, generically-worded responses that dominate the AI-journaling category today. The product's bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory.
23	
24	Cerne is explicitly not a mental-health or clinical tool. It makes no diagnostic claims, detects no risk signals (self-harm or suicidal ideation), and is positioned so a user processing their day through writing is never made to feel they are being monitored or clinically assessed. This is a product stance, not just a legal fence — current regulatory pressure on "AI companion" chatbots makes a non-clinical, non-companion framing a timing advantage as well as a safety one.
25	
26	Within this project's boundary, "done" means a working, fully tested iOS app that proves the RAG-memory differentiator end-to-end against the real (frozen) backend — covering capture, processing, chat, search, export, and account management — while leaving three named extension features (§5) as inert placeholders rather than attempting partial, half-working versions of them.

30	### 2.1 Jobs To Be Done
31	
32	`[ASSUMPTION: reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in docs/input — confirm or replace.]`
33	
34	The target user is a Portuguese-speaking adult already in the habit of processing their day through writing or talking to an AI, frustrated that neither medium remembers them between sessions.
35	
36	- **Functional** — capture what happened today in whichever mode is fastest in the moment (typing, speaking, or photographing a physical note/receipt-like artifact), without re-explaining context the app should already have.
37	- **Emotional** — feel understood in light of one's own history, not answered with a generic response that could apply to anyone.
38	- **Social/contextual** — maintain a private record that stays private; a quiet fear this persona carries is that a personal diary could be mined, sold, or silently reinterpreted as a mental-health signal.
39	- **Explicitly not** — seeking therapy, diagnosis, or a "companion" relationship with the AI; this user would be put off by anything implying they need clinical help.

41	### 2.2 Non-Users (v1)
42	
43	- Users seeking a clinical, diagnostic, or crisis-support tool — out of scope by design (§5).
44	- Users who need to edit or delete past Entries, or journal fully offline — Entries are immutable and writes are cloud-only (backend constraint; see §5, §8 OQ-5).
45	- Android users — platform is iOS, portrait-only, for this delivery.
46	- Users seeking AI-automated organization (auto-categorization, auto-extracted goals) — these exist only as static placeholders (§5).

48	### 2.3 Key User Journeys
49	
50	- **UJ-1. Mara unlocks the app and captures her day before bed.**
51	  - **Persona + context:** `[ASSUMPTION]` Mara, journals most nights, phone always nearby, wants capture to take under 30 seconds.
52	  - **Entry state:** app backgrounded since this morning (>5 min), biometric vault active.
53	  - **Path:** opens app → Tela 0 splash auto-advances → Tela 0.1 Biometria prompts Face ID → succeeds → Home/Chat. Taps "+" → Insertion Modal opens on the Texto tab → she switches to Áudio, records 40 seconds → recording stops → "Processando" → on-device transcription completes → "Transcrito" text shown → taps Salvar.
54	  - **Climax:** the Entry appears, saved, with no round-trip to a server required for the transcription step itself.
55	  - **Resolution:** modal closes, she's back on Home/Chat; the Entry now exists for RF07 (timeline) and RF06 (search) to surface later.
56	  - **Edge case:** Face ID fails twice → "Usar PIN" link → Tela 0.1b/0.1c PIN flow, no lockout (FR-5).
57	
58	- **UJ-2. Mara asks the assistant about a pattern she's noticed.**
59	  - **Entry state:** authenticated, on Home/Chat, has weeks of prior entries.
60	  - **Path:** types a question referencing something she wrote about weeks ago → sends → streaming response begins, grounded in RAG over her own Entries (not a generic answer) → response completes.
61	  - **Climax:** the response correctly surfaces something specific from her own history — the core differentiator (§1) made concrete.
62	  - **Resolution:** conversation continues naturally; she can keep chatting or start a new conversation from the side menu.
63	  - **Edge case:** the stream can drop mid-response, and separately her session can expire mid-conversation — either way she can recover (retry, or "Entrar novamente") without losing the thread of what she was saying (FR-2, FR-26).
64	
65	- **UJ-3. Mara saves something she said in chat as a proper journal entry.**
66	  - **Entry state:** mid-conversation, has just written a reflective message of her own.
67	  - **Path:** taps the bookmark affordance on her own message (never available on the AI's replies) → saving state shown → saved.
68	  - **Climax:** the message now exists as a real Entry (source=`chat`), reachable later from the timeline and search, without her having to retype it.
69	  - **Resolution:** chat continues uninterrupted either way.
70	  - **Edge case:** tapping save twice, or a save that fails, both leave the chat fully usable and recoverable (FR-29, FR-30).
71	
72	- **UJ-4. Mara looks for everything she wrote about feeling anxious before a specific event.**
73	  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros (timeline), has Entries from text, audio, and photo sources.
74	  - **Path:** types a word like "ansiedade" into the search bar → results return Entries that used related but different wording (e.g. "nervosismo") because the match is semantic, not literal → she narrows further with the filter sheet (date range, source) → active filters shown as removable chips.
75	  - **Climax:** she finds Entries she could not have found with exact-keyword search, from an origin (audio transcript) she'd forgotten she used.
76	  - **Resolution:** clears filters → full list restored without a screen reload.
77	  - **Edge case:** no results for the period → the screen's empty state, distinct from the "no entries at all" empty state (§4.5 FR-16), still offers a path back to capture.
78	
79	- **UJ-5. Mara exports a narrative summary of her last three months before a personal check-in with herself.**
80	  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros, taps the download icon.
81	  - **Path:** selects a period → export sheet shows "Pendente" → "Processando" → either "Concluído" (both PDF narrative and raw data downloadable) or, if only the AI narrative step failed, raw data remains downloadable while the narrative is marked unavailable — the job is never blocked end-to-end by a narrative failure.
82	  - **Climax:** she gets a readable, honest reflection of her last three months, or at minimum her raw data, every time she asks.
83	  - **Resolution:** closes the sheet via "Fechar."
84	  - **Edge case:** she picks a period with zero Entries → "Período vazio" state, no crash, no download offered (FR-37).
85	
86	- **UJ-6. Mara checks her settings dashboard, then eventually decides to leave.**
87	  - **Entry state:** on Configurações.
88	  - **Path:** dashboard renders a chart + narrative computed on demand; she edits her display name inline; much later, in a separate session, she decides to stop using the app and taps "Apagar conta," confirms in the red dialog.
89	  - **Climax:** her account and data are hard-deleted, consistent with the "this is genuinely mine to remove" expectation a journaling app sets.
90	  - **Resolution:** routed back to the Biometric Vault / login screen, same as logout (no dedicated confirmation screen exists for either flow — §8 OQ-4).
91	  - **Edge case:** dashboard has data but the AI-generated narrative specifically failed to generate — a distinct state from "zero entries," since the chart still renders (FR-39).

93	## 3. Glossary
94	
95	- **Entry** — A persisted journal record created via one of four sources: `manual` (text), `audio`, `photo`, or `chat` (via RF10). Immutable once created — no edit or delete operation exists. Always created through `POST /entries`.
96	- **Chat Session** — A persistent, named conversation thread with the AI assistant. A user may hold multiple sessions, switchable from the side menu.
97	- **Chat Message** — A single turn within a Chat Session; distinct from an Entry unless explicitly saved via RF10 (Save Chat Message as Entry).
98	- **Insertion Modal** — The bottom-sheet UI, opened from the "+" control on Home/Chat, through which all Entries are captured (Texto / Áudio / Foto tabs).
99	- **Sync Badge** — A per-Entry UI indicator with exactly three states: *Synchronizing*, *Synchronization error*, *Synchronized*. Derived entirely client-side from `Entry.updatedAt` and `Entry.serverRevision`; the backend has no `sync_status` field.
100	- **Insight** — An AI-generated message the assistant injects into a Chat Session unprompted, per RF08's trigger conditions.
101	- **Export Job** — An asynchronous job (RF05) producing a narrative PDF and/or raw-data download for a date period; tracked by independent `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) fields.
102	- **Dashboard** — The evolution chart + narrative text on the Configurações screen (RF09), computed on demand when the screen opens.
103	- **Biometric Vault** — The RF03 access barrier (Face ID / Touch ID / PIN) gating the whole app, validated on-device; has no backend counterpart beyond a stored preference.
104	- **Extension feature** `[ext]` — A feature named in requirements.md §2 as explicitly out of scope for this delivery; its UI exists only as an inert placeholder (§5).
105	- **Failure contract** — The `{ code, message, retryable }` shape returned by every backend error (13 closed codes; see §Cross-Cutting NFRs), consumed by every repository as `Either<Failure, T>`.

107	## Information Architecture
108	
109	- **Entrance/auth surfaces:** Splash (auto-advance) → Biometric Vault (Face ID/Touch ID, PIN fallback) → Login/Signup (single screen, toggled).
110	- **Home/Chat** is the base authenticated surface, with three overlays that can appear on top of it without navigating away: the Sessão Expirada overlay (FR-2), an offline banner (FR-27), and the Insertion Modal (§4.3). The side menu (☰), opened from here, leads to Chat Session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação `[ext]`.
111	- **Meus Registros (timeline)** carries its own overlay: the Export sheet (§4.10), plus an inline filter sheet and search bar (§4.6).
112	- **Configurações** hosts the dashboard (§4.11), inline profile editing, and the account-deletion confirmation dialog (§8 OQ-4).

150	### 4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)
151	
152	**Description:** A device-validated access barrier in front of all user data. Realizes UJ-1 (entry + edge case).
153	
154	#### FR-4: App-access gate
155	
156	The app requires Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any user data, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6).
157	
158	**Consequences (testable):**
159	- No screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable before authentication succeeds.
160	- No biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend — validation is 100% on-device.
161	
162	#### FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN
163	
164	A failed biometric attempt offers PIN entry as an alternative and never locks the user out of their own app.
165	
166	**Consequences (testable):**
167	- After a biometric failure, a PIN entry path is always reachable (Tela 0.1c).
168	- Repeated biometric failures that trigger an OS-level lockout are detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback rather than retried against the OS.
169	
170	#### FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout
171	
172	Returning to the app from the background after 5 minutes requires re-authentication; this value is fixed, not user-configurable.
173	
174	**Consequences (testable):**
175	- Resuming before 5 minutes elapsed does not prompt re-authentication.
176	- Resuming after 5 minutes always prompts re-authentication, regardless of any user setting.
177	
178	#### FR-7: Biometric preference persistence
179	
180	The user's choice to enable/disable biometric gating is saved server-side via `PATCH /account/settings` and survives app restarts (but not reinstalls).
181	
182	**Consequences (testable):**
183	- Disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method — the vault itself cannot be turned off entirely.

188	
189	**Description:** The single entry point for creating a journal Entry, in text, audio, or photo form, all through the Insertion Modal. Realizes UJ-1.
190	
191	#### FR-8: Text Entry capture
192	
193	A user can type free text in the Insertion Modal and save it as an Entry (source=`manual`).
194	
195	#### FR-9: Audio Entry capture
196	
197	A user can record audio in the Insertion Modal; the raw recording becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`audio`) once processed (RF02).

200

204	- All three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape — none is structurally special-cased after capture.
205	- Each call to `POST /entries` carries the correct `source` value for its modality.

208

217	### 4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)
218	
219	**Description:** Turns raw audio into text on-device, and raw photos into text via the backend, before an Entry is persisted. Realizes UJ-1.
220	
221	#### FR-12: On-device audio transcription
222	
223	Recorded audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend.
224	
225	**Consequences (testable):**
226	- Exactly four visible states occur in sequence or on failure: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
227	- No network call containing audio bytes is made at any point in this pipeline.
228	
229	#### FR-13: Backend OCR for photos
230	
231	A captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created.
232	
233	**Consequences (testable):**
234	- Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern: capture → processing OCR → recognized → (on failure) error with retry, photo never discarded.
235	- `OCR_NO_TEXT` (no extractable text found) is handled as a distinct, user-visible outcome, not a generic failure.
236	
237	**Notes:** Test material for both pipelines — sample audio, OCR test images, and expected transcription output — lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/`.

241	### 4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)
242	
243	**Description:** A chronological view of every Entry regardless of origin, each carrying a Sync Badge. Realizes UJ-1 (as the destination for captured entries) and UJ-4 (as the surface search/filter operates on).
244	
245	#### FR-14: Chronological Entry list
246	
247	All Entries, from any source, are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
248	
249	#### FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge
250	
251	Each Entry shows one of three Sync Badge states, derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` and local pending-write state — the backend exposes no `sync_status` field.
252	
253	**Consequences (testable):**
254	- A freshly created Entry shows "Synchronizing" until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then "Synchronized."
255	- A write that fails (network or any Failure-contract code) shows "Synchronization error" until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.
256	- The badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling (FR-17).
257	- `[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-6.
258	
259	#### FR-16: Empty-state handling
260	
261	With zero Entries, the screen shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.
262	
263	#### FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view
264	
265	If the session expires while viewing the timeline, the FR-2 overlay appears without crashing or losing scroll position.
266	
267	#### FR-18: Entry detail view
268	
269	A user can open a single Entry from the timeline to see its full content, via `GET /entries/:id`.
270	
271	**Consequences (testable):**
272	- Opening an Entry never mutates it — there is no edit affordance, consistent with Entries being immutable (§3 Glossary).
273	- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04), not a permission-denied code.
274	
275	**Feature-specific NFRs:** No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the three streams this screen composes (auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data) combine only through the domain layer, never via a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
